Arcades were a victim of circumstance. When they started out, home systems were not nearly as strong as the hardware inside of public cabinets (or they were, but were also ridiculously expensive as in the case of the Neo Geo home system) and console ports struggled to be authentic to the original. And they were doing well enough to be abundant-- liquor stores, pizza parlors, laundromats, and other assorted establishments had a machine or two. As the technology developed, home systems slowly started matching and then outdoing the cabinets, and that was before netplay and internet cafes became a factor as well. SNK had business misfortunes in 2000 and September 11th supposedly affected the ease of importing machines.

Since the 80s and 90s we've reached a point where the prettier games go straight home (sometimes with far more features and content than the arcade could provide), online play is a lot smoother than it used to be, a quarter doesn't stretch as far as it used to, arcade places had harder times affording newer cabinets and just weren't finding them particularly worth it (i.e. earning enough to cover costs). It's a sad way the times changed, as there was a certain charm of seeing the ways people played fighting games at the different arcades across town.
